Meanwhile, the opponent has Wasteland (x2), Lair of the Hydra, and Verdant Catacombs with relevant activated abilities that Pithing Needle could actually name. More importantly, Grindstone is available as a search option and is the key combo piece (with Painter's Servant, presumably in the deck). Lotus Petal would provide immediate mana acceleration to help cast cards in hand like Goblin Engineer or Phyrexian Dragon Engine. Mishra's Research Desk could provide card advantage. Any of these would be more useful than a Pithing Needle naming a creature with only a static ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Searched for Pithing Needle with Urza's Saga chapter III, intending to name Collector Ouphe to suppress its ability.
annotations.betterLine: Search for Lotus Petal to gain mana for casting Goblin Engineer (which can tutor Ensnaring Bridge from graveyard back to battlefield, or find other artifacts), or search for Grindstone as a combo piece. Pithing Needle naming Collector Ouphe is a complete whiff since the Ouphe's ability is static, not activated.

annotations.description: With Collector Ouphe on the opponent's board preventing artifact activated abilities, Soul-Guide Lantern is mostly a redundant second copy (ETB exile trigger is fine, but activated abilities are locked). More importantly, Libby already has a Soul-Guide Lantern on the battlefield that can be used as Goblin Welder fodder to swap for Ensnaring Bridge. Pithing Needle would have been more impactful - it could name Wasteland (opponent has two) to protect Libby's lands, or name Lair of the Hydra to prevent a creature-land threat, and its enter-the-battlefield name choice works through Collector Ouphe.

annotations.betterLine: Search for Pithing Needle naming Wasteland to protect lands from the opponent's two Wastelands, while using the existing Soul-Guide Lantern as Goblin Welder fodder to bring back Ensnaring Bridge

annotations.description: Passed with a full hand and plenty of mana available when Goblin Engineer could be cast to tutor an artifact to graveyard and develop the board. The reasoning incorrectly states Ensnaring Bridge is on the battlefield when it's clearly in the graveyard. With Goblin Welder already on board (creature ability, unaffected by Collector Ouphe), casting Goblin Engineer to find a key artifact and potentially welding Ensnaring Bridge or other artifacts into play would be a strong line. Additionally, Grindstone could be cast for 1 mana to put an artifact on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, incorrectly believing Ensnaring Bridge was already on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Goblin Engineer (using Mountain mana) to search library for a key artifact (like Painter's Servant for the Grindstone combo), then potentially use Goblin Welder to swap Soul-Guide Lantern for Ensnaring Bridge from graveyard if defense is needed.

annotations.description: Attacking Goblin Engineer (1/2) into Collector Ouphe (2/2) risks losing the Engineer for free. The opponent will almost certainly block with the 2/2, killing the 1/2 Engineer with no trade. While Ouphe currently shuts down Engineer's ability, the Engineer is still valuable as a future resource if Ouphe is removed. The reasoning also references Ensnaring Bridge and an empty hand, neither of which are true in this board state.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Goblin Engineer into a board with Collector Ouphe (2/2) that cleanly blocks and kills it.
annotations.betterLine: Don't attack. Keep Goblin Engineer back as a future resource for when Collector Ouphe is dealt with, allowing it to recur artifacts from the graveyard.

annotations.description: During combat, ESPN passed without activating Lair of the Hydra to animate it as an attacker. With 7+ lands available, they could have made a sizable Hydra creature and attacked alongside Collector Ouphe, pressuring the opponent's 14 life total against minimal blockers (just Goblin Engineer 1/2).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without activating Lair of the Hydra.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Lair of the Hydra for X=3 or X=4 to create a creature and attack with it alongside Collector Ouphe, dealing significant damage through or around the lone Goblin Engineer blocker.

annotations.description: Opponent has no untapped blockers (both Goblin Welder and Goblin Engineer are tapped). Qwen3L ESPN had 6 available mana sources (Bayou, 2 Forests, Bojuka Bog, 2 Wastelands) to activate Lair of the Hydra as a 5/5 creature and attack alongside Collector Ouphe for 7 total damage (bringing opponent from 12 to 5), but only dealt 2 damage with Collector Ouphe alone.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Collector Ouphe for 2 damage, not activating Lair of the Hydra.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Lair of the Hydra for X=5 (spending 6 mana) to create a 5/5 attacker, then attack with both Collector Ouphe and Lair of the Hydra for 7 total damage against an opponent with no untapped blockers.

annotations.description: Fetching Birds of Paradise (a mana dork) when the opponent is at 10 life with a dangerous Goblin Engineer/Welder artifact combo setup. Grist, the Hunger Tide could immediately -2 to destroy Goblin Engineer or Welder, disrupting the combo while providing ongoing value. Wight of the Reliquary would also be a huge threat (~7/7+ with 6 creature cards in graveyard). Birds provides incremental mana but doesn't address the board or apply pressure.

annotations.betterLine: Fetch Grist, the Hunger Tide to immediately -2 and destroy Goblin Engineer or Goblin Welder, disrupting the opponent's artifact recursion combo. Alternatively, Wight of the Reliquary as a massive beater that can also tutor utility lands.

With Bayou untapped, Qwen3L could play Birds of Paradise or Ignoble Hierarch (G), then cast Hogaak by convoking Ouphe (green for B/G) + the new dork (green for B/G) + delving 5 cards from graveyard. annotations.betterLine: Don't attack. Play Birds of Paradise or Ignoble Hierarch using Bayou, then cast Hogaak via convoke (tap Ouphe + new dork for the two B/G costs) and delve 5 cards. Hogaak attacks next turn for 8 trample damage.

annotations.description: Exiled Birds of Paradise, the only card that could produce white and blue mana needed for Atraxa, Grand Unifier in hand. Dryad Arbor is strictly worse to keep since it only produces green (which the board already has plenty of) and is a 1/1 with summoning sickness.

annotations.betterLine: In main phase, cast Ignoble Hierarch with Bayou, then cast Hogaak via convoke (tap Ignoble Hierarch) + delve 6 cards from graveyard, deploying a massive threat that threatens lethal next combat.

annotations.description: Collector Ouphe is tapped and ESPN has no untapped blockers. Libby could have attacked with both Goblin Welder (2/1 with Lavaspur Boots) and Goblin Engineer (1/2) for 3 unblocked damage. The reasoning incorrectly states the Ouphe could block.

annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Goblin Welder and Goblin Engineer for 3 free damage, since Collector Ouphe is tapped and there are no other potential blockers.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 8 life and Qwen3L ESPN has 7 untapped lands including Lair of the Hydra. Activating Lair as a 6/6 creature and attacking would deal massive damage (opponent can only chump with small creatures), putting them to 2 or forcing unfavorable blocks. Declining to activate Lair wastes a significant damage opportunity against a low-life opponent.

Additionally, Collector Ouphe prevents Goblin Welder's activated ability from being used anyway, so there's no reason to keep it untapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all available creatures for 2-3 free damage against an opponent with no untapped blockers

annotations.description: Goblin Welder's activated ability is a creature ability, NOT an artifact ability, so Collector Ouphe does not prevent it from activating. Libby could have activated Goblin Welder to sacrifice Pithing Needle (or another artifact) and return Painter's Servant from the graveyard to the battlefield, choosing blue. This would make Collector Ouphe blue, enabling Pyroblast to destroy it. With Ouphe removed, all artifact abilities unlock, allowing the Painter's Servant + Grindstone combo path. The reasoning incorrectly stated Ouphe 'silences' Goblin Welder and hallucinated 'Lightning Greaves' protecting the Ouphe.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, doing nothing, believing Goblin Welder was shut down by Collector Ouphe.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Goblin Welder targeting own Pithing Needle (controlled artifact) and Painter's Servant (artifact in graveyard), returning Painter's Servant choosing blue. Then cast Pyroblast targeting the now-blue Collector Ouphe to destroy it, unlocking all artifact abilities.

annotations.description: Libby has Painter's Servant and Pyroblast in hand. Playing Painter's Servant (naming blue) would make all permanents blue, allowing Pyroblast to destroy Collector Ouphe - the key hate piece preventing artifact activated abilities. Removing Ouphe would unlock Goblin Welder and enable the Painter-Grindstone combo win condition. Instead, Libby passed to preserve hand size for Ensnaring Bridge, but Bridge already blocks adequately at 4 cards in hand (after casting Servant + Pyroblast), and the opponent's creatures are small.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing any spells, citing Ensnaring Bridge hand-size concerns.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Painter's Servant (choosing blue), then cast Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe (now blue) to destroy it. This removes the artifact-hate piece, enables Goblin Welder's ability, and sets up the Painter-Grindstone combo. Hand would drop to 4 cards, still protecting via Bridge against creatures with power > 4.

annotations.description: Libby missed the line of casting Painter's Servant (choosing blue) which would make Collector Ouphe blue, then using Pyroblast or Red Elemental Blast to destroy it. This would remove the artifact-ability lock that has been paralyzing their entire game plan. They had plenty of mana (3 Mountains + Ancient Tomb) and all the pieces in hand (Painter's Servant + Pyroblast/REB).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without taking any action, reasoning (incorrectly) that there were no valid targets for Pyroblast and nothing useful to do.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Painter's Servant choosing blue (2 mana), then cast Pyroblast or Red Elemental Blast targeting Collector Ouphe (now blue) to destroy it, unlocking all artifact activated abilities including Goblin Welder.

annotations.description: Painter's Servant is the key combo piece with Grindstone (and with Pyroblast/Red Elemental Blast for removal). Choosing 'Blue' would make all permanents, spells, and cards blue in addition to their other colors, which would allow Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast to destroy any permanent (like Collector Ouphe) or counter any spell. It would also enable the Grindstone combo to mill the opponent's entire library since all cards would share the color blue. Choosing 'Red' does NOT enable Pyroblast/REB to target opposing permanents — those cards say 'if it's blue' not 'if it's red'. By choosing Red, the Painter's Servant does essentially nothing useful: Pyroblast destroys blue permanents and counters blue spells, and Red Elemental Blast targets blue permanents/spells. Making everything red doesn't help with any of these cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Red for Painter's Servant's color
annotations.betterLine: Choose Blue for Painter's Servant. This makes all permanents blue, enabling Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast to destroy Collector Ouphe and any other problematic permanent, and also enables the Grindstone combo to mill the opponent's entire library.

annotations.description: Painter's Servant is in the graveyard, not on the battlefield, so it doesn't make permanents any additional color. Casting Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe will do nothing because the Ouphe is green, not blue. The player incorrectly believes Painter's Servant is active and making things red/blue. This wastes a card for zero effect, and the Collector Ouphe continues to shut down the artifact plan.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Phyrexian Dragon Engine as a 2/2 double striker that could potentially block or apply pressure, or activate Goblin Welder (though Collector Ouphe prevents artifact activated abilities). The correct plan would be to recognize Painter's Servant needs to be returned to the battlefield first before Pyroblast can work on non-blue permanents.

annotations.description: Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe will do nothing because Ouphe is green, not blue, and there's no Painter's Servant on the battlefield to change its color. This wastes a card for zero effect.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pyroblast targeting Collector Ouphe (a non-blue permanent) before getting Painter's Servant into play.
annotations.betterLine: First activate Goblin Welder (a creature, unaffected by Collector Ouphe) to swap a dispensable artifact (like Pithing Needle) for Painter's Servant from the graveyard. With Painter's Servant in play choosing blue, Collector Ouphe becomes blue, and THEN Pyroblast would successfully destroy it.

annotations.description: At 2 HP with opponent at 14 HP, Libby declined to attack with any creatures despite having Phyrexian Dragon Engine (2/2 double strike = 4 damage unblocked), Painter's Servant (1/3), and Goblin Welder (1/1) against only one blocker (Collector Ouphe 2/2). annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (or at minimum Phyrexian Dragon Engine and Painter's Servant) to deal 4-5 damage through the single blocker, pressuring the opponent's 14 life total while the combo is locked by Ouphe
